Read every kind of metadata a file carries

Source: R/readMetadata.R
readMetadata.Rd

Reads the embedded metadata of an audio file, whatever format that metadata is in and whatever container the file is: GUANO, Wildlife Acoustics wamd, Broadcast Wave bext, iXML and the INFO list from a wave file, the AudioMoth comment, ID3 from an MP3 file or from a wave file that holds a tag in a chunk, and Vorbis comments from a FLAC or Ogg file. A file holding none of them gives an empty result rather than an error. A wave file over 4 GiB, written in the RF64 or BW64 form, is read as any other, and named by that form.

Usage

readMetadata(x, filename = TRUE)

Arguments

x

Path to an audio file, a Wave object with metadata attached, or a raw vector holding a file

filename

Whether to read the name of the file as well as its contents. TRUE works the format out from the name, FALSE reads only what is inside the file, and the name of one of parseFilename()'s formats reads the name as that, which settles a name the package could not have settled on its own.

Value

An audioMetadata object. file and container are always there, so its length says nothing about whether the file carried any metadata: ask length(x$sources) for that, or length(x$fields) for whether anything was read that this package has a normalised name for.

Details

A recording commonly carries more than one of these formats, written by the device that made it and by whatever software has handled it since, and the same fact under a different name in each. The result therefore holds both what each format said and one normalised record built from all of them:

file

The path the metadata was read from, or NA

container

The kind of file it was read from, read from the bytes of the file rather than from its name, or NA where it is not one this package recognises

fields

The normalised record (see below)

sources

The formats that were found, each as the object its own reader gives, named guano, wamd, audiomoth, bext, ixml, wavInfo, xmp, disp, id3, vorbisComment and filename. A format the file does not carry is left out.

unparsed

The identifiers of any chunks the file holds that carry metadata this package cannot read, such as the proprietary block an editor leaves behind. Knowing they are there is worth more than passing over them in silence.

The normalised record

fields holds whichever of datetime, make, model, serial, firmware, software, prefix, microphone, title, species, recordist, comment, note, licence, url, location, elevation, collection, project and take the file said anything about. location is a latitude and a longitude in degrees, and datetime is a POSIXct wherever the file gave enough to make one.

Where two formats say the same thing, the one that is believed is the first of GUANO, wamd, the AudioMoth comment, bext, iXML, the INFO list, ID3, Vorbis comments and the filename: a format written for bioacoustics is trusted over one written for broadcast, and anything written inside the file over anything read from its name. Nothing is thrown away by this, as sources still holds what every format said.

A field that holds only a year gives no datetime, as it has no month or day to make one with; the year can still be read from the source that gave it. Species are taken only from a format that names a species as such, and never guessed at from a title.

A time in an ID3 tag that names no zone is read as UTC, which version 2.4 of the format says every time in it is, rather than as a wall clock in the zone of the session, as one in an INFO list, an XMP packet or a Vorbis comment is read. It comes back in UTC, so it prints as the tag wrote it whatever the zone of the session, and it may stop at the hour, as the format allows.

Reading from a name

filename reads the filename conventions that parseFilename() knows, and is the one source nothing outranks: where the file itself said nothing, what its name says is the whole answer. Pass filename=FALSE to read only what is inside the file.

Because nothing outranks it, a reading the name left in doubt gives no datetime. A name of nothing but digits is read as a date or as a count of seconds, and a collection that numbers its records gives names of exactly that shape, so a date taken from one would often be a confident wrong answer with nothing beside it to correct it.

Where you know what your own files are named by, say so: filename takes the name of a filename format as well as TRUE or FALSE, as in filename = "YYYYMMDD". Naming it settles what those digits mean, so the date is read and used rather than passed over as a guess. The formats are those parseFilename() lists.

A TSA name gives a species and a collection. That corpus commonly holds no embedded metadata at all, so for those recordings its name is the only thing there is to read.

See also

The readers for one format at a time: guano(), wamd(), bext(), ixml(), wavInfo(), id3(), vorbisComment() and audiomothWave(). audioMetadata<- attaches a reading to a Wave object.

Examples

f <- system.file("extdata/AUDIOMOTH_GUANO.WAV", package="sonicscrewdriver")
m <- readMetadata(f)
m$fields$model
#> [1] "AudioMoth"
m$sources$guano
#> GUANO|Version          1.0
#> Make                   Open Acoustic Devices
#> Model                  AudioMoth
#> Serial                 247AB4055C7B17DB
#> Firmware Version       AudioMoth-Firmware-Basic (1.11.0)
#> Timestamp              2026-05-14T20:06:00Z
